runtimeUpdate.purpose: Support all twelve published answer choices on Mock C Paper 2 Question 20.
changes: Compiler and question audit accept two to twelve choices and validate the answer against the actual option count.
Newly compiled player displays and restores K and L.
Parent answer capture and history presentation retain and display K/L choices.

independentReview.author: /root
independentReview.scope: Independent static and focused non-browser review of exact 12-option support changes. The author and reviewer are distinct. This review does not approve authored Paper 2 mathematics or claim completed production/browser checks.
findings: Compared every listed file against the actual repository and confirmed those baseline bytes match qa/baseline.json. Production deltas are limited to the player letter set, compiler/audit limits and future K/L answer-log acceptance/display.
Compiler and content audit accept 11/K and 12/L only when the requested answer option exists; they continue to reject 13/M, 12/M, 11/L and 10/K. No malformed-capacity check was removed.

Player option rendering, correct-option lookup and restored selected-option validation share the widened letters constant. Existing per-question option-length validation remains in place, so M or an unavailable letter is rejected.

App/history changes only expand one answer-letter regular expression in each file. First-answer retention, latest-answer tracking, first/after numerical calculations, stored attempts, authentication, schema and permissions algorithms are unchanged.

Focused tests exercise K/L rendering and accessible labels, scoring and state resume, rejection of malformed M, fixed first marks on retry, parent first/latest answer logging, and history display without score mutation.
P2 proposal structural audit now passes all47 question records with116 concepts and126 syllabus clauses; exact question/concept/relationship fingerprints are current.

gaps.reason: One prime-exponent/converse transfer was reviewed. Generic divisibility proof questions do not repeat the square-to-factor exponent operation closely enough for further slots.
One close signed-inequality classification was reviewed. Extra general algebra questions would not add another defensible order-preservation variation.
One precise squared-trigonometric-sum identity transfer was reviewed. It has an additional proof/sign audit; no close official cube-sum calculation was found.
One directly related monotonicity/derivative necessary-condition question was reviewed. Integral calculation alone would not rehearse whole-function counterexamples.

One stationary-point implication transfer was reviewed. No close official comparison with this stronger second-derivative coefficient threshold was found; a derivative computation alone is insufficient as a variant.
Two fractional-power derivative sign tasks were reviewed, with their domain/prefactor differences explicit. No unrelated calculus filler was added.
One exact shared-count/sole-truth variation was reviewed. Different truth-teller arrangements do not automatically repeat the same labelled-integer operation.
Two remainder-evaluation transfers were reviewed. No third close linear-remainder recovery question was found.

No sufficiently close official high-power integer equation requiring factor-pair enumeration and restoration of all signed ordered pairs was found. Routine polynomial root questions do not replace this integer operation.
One distinguishing-feedback information problem was reviewed. Generic truth-table or extremum exercises would not provide the same observation/ambiguity operation.
Three distinct official SSA problems were reviewed, with one-triangle classification versus two-branch area comparisons explicitly distinguished.

No close official counterexample to this all-real symmetric-average-implies-linearity claim was found. Integration cancellation or an unrelated functional substitution would not reproduce its required counterexample operation.
One direct whole-real order-transformation variation was reviewed. Its exponents and sufficiency-only requirement differ from this equivalence question; no exact reprint is used.
Three official cubic turning-height problems were reviewed, with one versus three roots and the logical containment direction made explicit.
Two exact-comparison/surd transfers were reviewed. Neither is claimed to reproduce every log/GP/surd operation of the mixed original.
One direct transformation-order identity question and one ordered-transformation prerequisite were reviewed. Routine translations alone would not add a full identity variation.

One reciprocal-integer-pair counting transfer was reviewed, with its polygon setup and bounded-enumeration route distinguished from the original shifted-factor route. No unrelated integer counting filler was used.
One two-parameter quadratic-sign region transfer was reviewed. It adds a discriminant setup rather than a derivative, and does not pretend to include the original area calculation.

No close official variable-step integer sequence requiring every attainable transition count through a fixed checkpoint was found. AP/GP sums, deterministic recurrence cycles and unrelated bound constructions are not variants.
Three geometry-guarantee/counterexample transfers were reviewed. Their quadrilateral classes and scale constraints are explicitly distinguished from the original four-small-triangle proof.

followupAvailability.policy: Fewer than three are offered when the reviewed official bank has no further defensible match; no unrelated filler is added.

result: No unresolved release blocker for these exact reviewed files. This is evidence of content and runtime checks, not a promise of an examination score.
